response.markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize a small, controlled change: **a uniform-to-moderate lexical-negative curriculum within the corrected HSTU**. Its benefits remain hypotheses requiring host validation.

**Insights from the starting point and diagnosis**

1. Industrial has the largest measured training ranking-error rate, 5.05%. Improving discrimination is plausible, but training margins do not establish validation performance.
2. Users reject broad thematic matches and unsupported equipment or project assumptions. Contrasting superficially similar items could teach finer distinctions, although lexical similarity cannot establish compatibility.
3. Users also report stale interests. Missing paired-context effects prevent attributing this behavior to deficient recency sensitivity; negative sampling alone may not resolve it.

**Insights from related work**

1. HSTU uses multi-negative sampled softmax [1]. This makes uniform multi-negative training the essential family-consistent control.
2. R²NS motivates uniform warm-start followed by harder stochastic sampling [2]. Its evidence supports curriculum design, not lexical mining specifically.
3. HSTU-BLaIR motivates textual information [3]. Its pretrained representations are prohibited here, so title-based candidate mining must use permitted local text.

**Framework and directions**

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discrimination | HSTU sampled softmax | Uniform multi-negative control | Generalization |
| Confusable alternatives | R²NS curriculum | Moderate lexical negatives | False negatives |
| Temporal relevance | HSTU temporal bias [1] | Learned timestamp-gap bias | Missing context-effect evidence |

**Candidate assessment**

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each pair states a positive and negative consideration.

- **Uniform multi-negative loss: 2/7/5/8/2.** Originality: clean baseline / established; potential: scalable / limited novelty; user: finer ranking / indirect purpose matching; model: targets separation / training already strong; difficulty: loss-only change / memory cost.
- **Moderate lexical curriculum: 5/8/8/8/4.** Originality: task-specific combination / established components; potential: sharper distinctions / false negatives; user: targets thematic substitutes and unsupported equipment matches / cannot verify intent; model: challenges weak separation / benefit unmeasured; difficulty: training-only mining / exclusion bookkeeping.
- **Learned temporal bias: 3/7/7/4/6.** Originality: family-consistent / existing mechanism; potential: adaptive recency / sparse timestamps; user: targets stale and broad interests / compatibility unresolved; model: measurable context effects / supplied effects absent; difficulty: compact bias / interface changes.

**Selected algorithm**

Use titles/descriptions to construct moderate-similarity neighbor pools with TF–IDF, preserving identifiers, numbers and units. Warm-start with 32 uniform negatives; subsequently replace up to eight with randomly sampled moderate lexical neighbors. These are initial hyperparameters, not validated optima.

```text
for each causal training position:
    exclude padding, target, and user's training positives
    draw 32 unique uniform negatives
    after warm-start, gradually replace at most 8
        with moderate lexical neighbors of the positive
    optimize sampled softmax through the same HSTU
```

This explicitly targets broad substitutes and unsupported equipment/project matches through harder discrimination, and Industrial's measured ranking errors. Compatibility gains remain unproven. Match negative count and training limits against the uniform control; select using fixed macro validation HR@10. Preserve all routing, seeds, diagnostic interfaces, left-padding readout, and one checkpoint per category. No lexical score enters inference.

idea.description: Train the corrected HSTU with a uniform-to-moderate lexical-negative curriculum, keeping one independently trained model per category. Contrast training positives against superficially related alternatives to address broad thematic substitutions and unsupported equipment or project matches.
idea.motivation: Industrial has a measured 5.05% training negative-beats-positive rate, while qualitative feedback identifies insufficient discrimination between broad relevance and a supported next choice. These observations motivate harder training comparisons but do not demonstrate that lexical negatives improve validation HR@10 or actual compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only permitted titles/descriptions to build sparse TF–IDF neighbor pools; preserve model identifiers, numbers and units. Start with 32 uniform negatives and a five-epoch warm-start; ramp lexical replacements to eight by epoch 20 as an initial hypothesis. Exclude padding, reserved IDs, the positive and all known training positives; deduplicate and backfill uniformly. Restrict lexical candidates to a moderate similarity band rather than nearest duplicates. Use ordinary mixed-negative sampled cross-entropy and document its sampling distribution; do not claim an unbiased full-catalog likelihood. Keep inference architecture unchanged, with the predictor writer reproducing the trained HSTU and loading one checkpoint per category. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView and diagnosis interfaces; retain the original B x L diagnostic negative input and sample extra negatives internally during training. Read the greatest nonzero sequence position. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], artifacts under the trial directory, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Compare against uniform-only training with the same negative count and limits within the shared budget. Preserve the host evaluator and all four datasets; report no unmeasured gains.
idea.pseudocode:
Build local lexical neighbor pools from permitted item text.
For each epoch, set lexical_count = min(8, floor(8 * max(0, epoch - 5) / 15)).
For each of 200 training batches:
  Compute causal HSTU features for the existing left-padded sequences.
  For each valid target position:
    Exclude all known user training positives and reserved IDs.
    Draw lexical_count unique moderate lexical neighbors of the target.
    Backfill to 32 unique negatives with uniform draws.
  Minimize cross-entropy over the positive and its sampled negatives.
Evaluate only through the authorized validation procedure.
Retain one selected checkpoint per category; deploy its matching predictor.

originality.positive: Combines a family-consistent multi-negative objective with a restrained lexical curriculum tailored to the observed confusion patterns.
originality.negative: Curriculum sampling and lexical neighbors are established components; the combination is incremental.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled result could motivate better false-negative handling and purpose-sensitive training without additional inference cost.
future_potential.negative: Lexical overlap may emphasize superficial similarity, and unobserved relevant items remain potential false negatives.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes are concentrated in offline candidate construction, training sampling and loss computation; the inference backbone stays intact.
code_difficulty.negative: Sparse mining, user-level exclusions, unique sampling and bounded GPU memory require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU and provides architectural precedent for relative positional and temporal attention biases.
Uses multi-negative sampled softmax, supporting a family-consistent uniform-negative control.
limitations: Does not establish the optimal negative count or lexical curriculum for the four target datasets.
Published results do not establish gains under this pinned evaluation.

related_work.title: [2] R²NS
contributions: Supports uniform warm-start followed by progressively harder stochastic negative sampling.
Motivates avoiding immediate selection of the hardest unobserved items.
limitations: Does not directly validate lexical-neighbor sampling with HSTU.
Hard unobserved items may be false negatives.

related_work.title: [3] HSTU-BLaIR
contributions: Provides evidence that textual representations can complement HSTU on its evaluated datasets.
limitations: Its pretrained representations are outside the permitted resources.
Retains uniform item-ID sampling and therefore supplies no direct evidence for lexical negative mining.
